quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The economist said, "Inflation has been rising steadily since January."
options: The economist said that inflation has been rising steadily since January.
The economist said that inflation had been rising steadily since January.
The economist said that inflation had risen steadily since January.
quests.correctAnswer: The economist said that inflation had been rising steadily since January.
quests.sentence: The economist said, "Inflation has been rising steadily since January."
quests.hint: Compare 'had been rising' with 'had risen' carefully — one keeps the ongoing sense of the original, the other doesn't.
quests.explanation: 'Has been rising' (present perfect continuous, an ongoing trend) backshifts to 'had been rising', preserving the continuous, ongoing meaning; 'had risen' loses that ongoing sense.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Hiroshi said, "I was writing the report when the power went out."
options: Hiroshi said that he wrote the report when the power had gone out.
Hiroshi said that he was writing the report when the power went out.
Hiroshi said that he had been writing the report when the power had gone out.
quests.correctAnswer: Hiroshi said that he had been writing the report when the power had gone out.
quests.sentence: Hiroshi said, "I was writing the report when the power went out."
quests.hint: Compare all three options carefully — only one keeps both the background action and the interrupting event correctly distinguished.
quests.explanation: 'Was writing' (background action) backshifts to 'had been writing', and 'went out' (the interrupting event) backshifts to 'had gone out'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Chidinma said, "I have lived in this city for ten years."
options: Chidinma said that she has lived in that city for ten years.
Chidinma said that she had lived in that city for ten years.
Chidinma said that she lived in that city for ten years.
quests.correctAnswer: Chidinma said that she had lived in that city for ten years.
quests.sentence: Chidinma said, "I have lived in this city for ten years."
quests.hint: Compare 'had lived' with the simple past 'lived' — one preserves the sense of an ongoing state up to a point, the other only suggests a finished period.
quests.explanation: 'Have lived' (present perfect, ongoing up to now) backshifts to 'had lived', preserving that same sense one step further back in time.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Bianca told Farida, "Your idea is better than mine."
options: Bianca told Farida that her idea was better than hers.
Bianca told Farida that Farida's idea was better than Bianca's.
Bianca told Farida that her idea was better than her own.
quests.correctAnswer: Bianca told Farida that her idea was better than hers.
quests.sentence: Bianca told Farida, "Your idea is better than mine."
quests.hint: The pronoun 'her' appears twice with different meanings here — think about which idea belongs to whom.
quests.explanation: 'Your' (Farida's idea) becomes 'her' referring to Farida, and 'mine' (Bianca's idea) becomes 'hers' referring to Bianca.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Emeka told his father, "You always believed in me, and I'll never forget that."
options: Emeka told his father that he always believed in him and that he would never forget that.
Emeka told his father that his father had always believed in him and that Emeka would never forget that.
Emeka told his father that he had always believed in him and that he would never forget that.
quests.correctAnswer: Emeka told his father that he had always believed in him and that he would never forget that.
quests.sentence: Emeka told his father, "You always believed in me, and I'll never forget that."
quests.hint: Both 'he' pronouns need care — one refers to the father, the other to Emeka — but the natural way to report this uses pronouns for both, not repeated names.
quests.explanation: 'You' (the father) becomes 'he', 'me' (Emeka) becomes 'him', and 'I' (Emeka) becomes 'he' again — natural reported speech uses pronouns once the context is clear, not repeated names.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Yuna said to her twin sister, "People always confuse us for each other."
options: Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused her for her sister.
Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused us for each other.
Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused them for each other.
quests.correctAnswer: Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused them for each other.
quests.sentence: Yuna said to her twin sister, "People always confuse us for each other."
quests.hint: 'Us' refers to both twins together — when reported, it becomes a pronoun for that same pair, not a comparison between two separate people.
quests.explanation: 'Us' becomes 'them', referring to both twins together, and 'confuse' backshifts to 'confused'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The trainer said, "You should try doing squats before running."
options: The trainer advised me trying doing squats before running.
The trainer advised me to try doing squats before running.
The trainer suggested me to try doing squats before running.
quests.correctAnswer: The trainer advised me to try doing squats before running.
quests.sentence: The trainer said, "You should try doing squats before running."
quests.hint: 'Advised' takes an infinitive after the object, while 'suggested' never takes an object directly before an infinitive.
quests.explanation: 'Advised' correctly takes 'me to try', while 'suggested me to try' is a common but incorrect pattern, since 'suggested' cannot be followed directly by an object and an infinitive.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The coach said, "Why don't you try stretching before the game?"
options: The coach suggested to try stretching before the game.
The coach advised trying stretching before the game.
The coach suggested trying stretching before the game.
quests.correctAnswer: The coach suggested trying stretching before the game.
quests.sentence: The coach said, "Why don't you try stretching before the game?"
quests.hint: Recall which verb pattern fits 'suggested' — a gerund, not an infinitive.
quests.explanation: 'Suggested' takes a gerund ('trying'), not an infinitive ('to try'), and this phrasing ('why don't you...?') fits 'suggested' rather than 'advised'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The dietitian said, "I recommend eating more vegetables."
options: The dietitian recommended to eat more vegetables.
The dietitian recommended eating more vegetables.
The dietitian suggested to eat more vegetables.
quests.correctAnswer: The dietitian recommended eating more vegetables.
quests.sentence: The dietitian said, "I recommend eating more vegetables."
quests.hint: 'Recommended', like 'suggested', is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.
quests.explanation: 'Recommend eating' becomes 'recommended eating', keeping the gerund pattern; 'recommended to eat' is a common incorrect pattern.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The tour guide said, "We'll spend the morning here and the afternoon at the museum across town."
options: The tour guide said that they would spend the morning here and the afternoon at the museum across town.

The tour guide said that they will spend the morning there and the afternoon at the museum across town.

quests.sentence: The tour guide said, "We'll spend the morning here and the afternoon at the museum across town."
quests.hint: Only the first 'here' refers to the current location — the second location ('across town') doesn't need a place-word change since it's already named.
quests.explanation: 'Here' becomes 'there' since it refers to the guide's current location, while 'across town' stays the same because it's already a specific, named place.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The email said, "Please arrive at the venue by 9 AM; doors open at 8:30."

The email asked attendees to arrive at the venue by 9 AM and said that doors would open at 8:30.

quests.sentence: The email said, "Please arrive at the venue by 9 AM; doors open at 8:30."
quests.hint: Compare backshifting 'open' to 'opened' versus using 'would open' — this describes a fixed schedule, not a future intention.
quests.explanation: 'Open' backshifts to 'opened' as a simple fact about the schedule, not 'would open', which would suggest uncertainty about the future.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Noelle said, "I'll be at the office until 6, then home after that."
options: Noelle said that she will be at the office until 6, then home after that.
Noelle said that she would be at the office until 6, then home after that.
Noelle said that she would be at the office until 6, then home after then.

quests.sentence: Noelle said, "I'll be at the office until 6, then home after that."
quests.hint: 'After that' is already a general connector, not a specific time word like 'today' or 'now' — it doesn't need to change.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The manager said, "Let's avoid making the same mistake again."
options: The manager suggested avoid making the same mistake again.
The manager suggested to avoid making the same mistake again.
The manager suggested avoiding making the same mistake again.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager suggested avoiding making the same mistake again.
quests.sentence: The manager said, "Let's avoid making the same mistake again."
quests.hint: 'Avoid' itself is always followed by a gerund, and 'suggested' is too — check both verbs.
quests.explanation: 'Suggested avoiding' is correct because 'suggested' takes a gerund; 'avoid' also always takes a gerund ('avoid making'), never an infinitive.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, "I want everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class."

The teacher said that she wanted everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class.

quests.hint: 'Want' takes an object plus an infinitive, unlike 'suggested', which never takes an object directly before a verb.
quests.explanation: 'Want' correctly takes 'everyone to finish' (object + infinitive); 'suggested everyone to finish' is not a valid pattern for 'suggested'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Anton said, "I don't mind waiting a few extra minutes."

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Bashir said, "I broke my arm skiing last winter, and it's still a bit stiff."

Bashir said that he broke his arm skiing last winter and that it is still a bit stiff.

quests.sentence: Bashir said, "I broke my arm skiing last winter, and it's still a bit stiff."
quests.hint: Compare the two clauses carefully: one describes a finished past event, and the other describes a present, ongoing condition being reported.
quests.explanation: 'Broke' (a completed event) becomes 'had broken', but 'is still stiff' (a current state) still backshifts to 'was still stiff' once fully reported, and 'last winter' becomes 'the previous winter'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The travel guide said, "The museum is closed on Mondays."

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The supervisor said, "Don't submit the form without a signature."

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The landlord said, "Tenants shouldn't leave without giving notice."

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The mechanic said, "This could be a problem with the battery."
options: The mechanic said that that could be a problem with the battery.
The mechanic said that this could be a problem with the battery.

quests.sentence: The mechanic said, "This could be a problem with the battery."
quests.hint: 'Could' expressing a guess or possibility is already a past-time form and stays the same — don't confuse it with 'had to', which implies certainty or obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Could' (possibility) stays unchanged since it's already a past-time modal form, and 'this' becomes 'that'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The employee said, "I can finish this task by myself."

quests.explanation: 'Can' (ability) backshifts to 'could', and 'this' becomes 'that'; 'must' would incorrectly suggest an obligation rather than a capability.

quests.sentence: The teacher said, "Students must submit their essays by Friday."
quests.hint: This 'must' expresses a firm requirement — compare it with a modal that would suggest it's merely optional.
quests.explanation: 'Must' (obligation) backshifts to 'had to'; 'could' would incorrectly suggest submitting was optional rather than required.

quests.explanation: 'This' becomes 'that', 'has been tested' becomes 'had been tested', and 'holds up' backshifts to 'held up' since it's being reported as part of the scientist's overall claim.
